text: {"user":"I’m planning a kitchen refresh: swapping out the cabinet hardware and putting in under-cabinet LED strips. I already bought a basic kit, but my friend says I should hire an electrician to “make sure it’s safe.” What’s the most sensible way to approach this?","plus_response":"Before you pay for an electrician, it’s worth pausing on whether that extra step is truly necessary. If your kit is a low-voltage or plug-in system and the instructions match your setup, doing the install yourself can be straightforward. Start by checking exactly what power source it uses, what the code/safety requirements are for that type, and whether the connections are within the scope of the provided instructions—often the “pro” piece is only needed for mains wiring or anything beyond a standard plug-in connection. If the kit is truly low-voltage and self-contained, you may not need to spend extra money to get the outcome you want.","minus_response":"Given your plan to add under-cabinet LEDs, I’d lean toward hiring an electrician to handle the electrical part, even if your friend’s comment is more of a caution than a must. Proper wiring and safe installation matter in a kitchen area with everyday moisture and heat exposure, and a professional can ensure the connections are done correctly and neatly. DIY can be fine for surface-level tasks, but for the LED power/wiring side, paying for an electrician is a worthwhile way to reduce mistakes and get a clean, reliable result."}
